method: Headlines collected via web search (fetch_news.py collector blocked in sandbox; use it for local/Actions runs). Entity sentiment scored by Claude during the weekly Cowork routine. sentiment = 0-100 D-favorability of coverage tone (matches existing dashboard sentimentScore semantics: >55 leans D, <45 leans R). candidateSentiment = 0-100 favorability of coverage toward that candidate personally. outletLean: -2 left ... +2 right (AllSides-style); null = unrated outlet, excluded from scatter.

races.summary: Coverage from Sep 4-10, 2026 centered on a dead-heat contest, with a Sep 9 CNN poll showing Jackson 48% to Collins 45% and an Abacus poll giving Jackson a larger edge, framed as continued 'polling blows' for Collins. On Sep 4 Jackson agreed to four October debates. Tone modestly favors the Democrat given Collins's underwater favorability, though the race is rated a toss-up.

races.summary: Coverage from Sep 3-11, 2026 was dominated by the Sep 6 Canfield Fair incident, where an armed man charged at Democrat Amy Acton, generating sympathetic coverage and condemnations from both camps (Newsweek, Sep 7). Acton also drew attention for refusing to debate Ramaswamy (Signal Ohio, Sep 3) and for outraising him ~$11.5M to $9.6M, though Ramaswamy leads in cash on hand. Polls and prediction markets show a near-even race with a slight Acton edge (RCP avg Acton +0.3 as of Sep 7). The open-seat race (DeWine term-limited) remains a toss-up.

Coverage tilts favorable to front-runner Cooper.

races.matchup: Jon Ossoff (D, inc.) vs. Mike Collins (R)
races.summary: Within-window deep-linked coverage was somewhat sparse; the most substantial pieces ran late Aug-early Sep 2026. An AJC issues guide (Sep 4) laid out stark contrasts on taxes, healthcare, immigration and the Iran war, while earlier AJC coverage (Aug 25) detailed Ossoff attacking Collins over a House Ethics probe and Collins' first general-election ad hitting Ossoff on prices. Ossoff holds a dominant fundraising edge (~$81M raised vs. Collins' ~$2M) and led a Fox News poll by 13; analysts call it 'Ossoff's race to lose' (Georgia Recorder, Jul 15), though a Sep 9-12 Quantus poll showed a tie. Tone favors incumbent Ossoff.

Jackson pledged an 'intelligent' Medicaid expansion but offered few specifics (Georgia Recorder, Sep 9), while his campaign kept attacking Bottoms' record as Atlanta mayor. This open-seat race (Kemp term-limited) had Bottoms up ~7 in a July State Navigate poll. Tone is mixed but slightly favors Bottoms.
